ru: Я подтверди́л бы э́то под прися́гой.
Ты бы поду́мала об э́том ещё раз.
en: You should think about it once more.
note: «Ты бы + past» with no protasis is the advisory construction ('you should…'), not a conditional; this also clears the 'would think' frame collision with the imperfective partner.
Collision is frame-only against a participle and a gerund sentence whose content differs completely; 'without thinking' is the only natural English here.

en_alt: He thought it over and agreed.
note: Equally valid rendering of the momentary perfective; keeps the word-bank from rejecting it.
Frame-only collision with «Ду́май о бу́дущем.»; the rest of the sentence ('carefully before answering') is a clear cue.

ru: Я поду́маю над твои́м предложе́нием за́втра.
Ско́ро я подхвачу́ ма́ленькую дочь на ру́ки.
note: 'Scoop up' is the natural English for подхвати́ть на́ руки; the gloss 'to catch' still covers the sense.

ru: Е́сли бы знал слова́, я подхвати́л бы мело́дию.
en_alt: If I knew the words, I would join in the tune.
If I knew the words, I would take up the tune.
note: Adds the Russian clause order and the 'take up' rendering used by the sibling sentences.

ru: Во вре́мя у́жина официа́нт бу́дет подходи́ть к ва́шему сто́лику.
en: During dinner, the waiter will be coming over to your table.
note: бу́дет подходи́ть is the imperfective compound future (repeated approaches through the meal); the flat 'will come over' reads as one occasion.

ru: Лю́ди подходи́ли к сце́не оди́н за други́м.

en_alt: Don't go near the edge!
note: The idiomatic English warning; the literal 'approach' stays as en_gb.

ru: Ты подхо́дишь к до́му ка́ждый ве́чер?
Я подхожу́ к до́му ка́ждый ве́чер.
Я подходи́ла бы к нему́ осторо́жнее.
note: Habitual 'would approach' is right for the imperfective; the frame collision leaves a clear cue (I/more carefully vs you/first), and the partner is the side to review.

ru: Е́сли бы́ли де́ньги, я пое́хала бы на мо́ре.
en_alt: If I had the money, I would go to the seaside.
note: Adds the Russian clause order as an accepted answer.

ru: Ско́ро ты пое́дешь на велосипе́де в парк.
en_alt: Soon you will set off for the park by bike.
note: 'Set off for X' is the standard English collocation; accepted alongside 'set off to'.

en_alt: They set off for the seaside in summer.
note: 'Set off for X' is the standard English collocation.

en_alt: I will set off for the village tomorrow.
note: 'Set off for X' is the standard English collocation.

ru: Я пожале́ю де́нег на тако́е де́ло.
note: 'Begrudge' is a sense the gloss 'to feel sorry' does not cover, and the affirmative пожале́ю де́нег is odd — this collocation is normally negated («не пожале́ю де́нег»); a human should decide whether to widen the gloss or reword the Russian.

ru: Ско́ро ты пожале́ешь о свое́м реше́нии.
ru_new: Ско́ро ты пожале́ешь о своём реше́нии.
note: Prepositional of своё is своём with ё; «свое́м» is a misspelling. Token count unchanged, so any inflect index is unaffected. English is fine as it stands.

ru: Ты бы пожале́л об э́тих слова́х.

en: You will be sorry about this yet.
en_alt: You will regret this yet.
note: ещё here is the emphatic 'yet', not 'still' — 'you will still feel sorry' wrongly implies you already do.

en_alt: Will you regret this?
note: пожале́ть о чём-л. is standardly 'regret'; accepted alongside the gloss-matching wording.

ru: При встре́че мы пожмём друг дру́гу ру́ки.
en_alt: When we meet we will shake each other's hands.
note: Renders друг дру́гу explicitly; both are natural.

ru: Я пожа́л бы ему́ ру́ку с ра́достью.
Он пожа́л мне ру́ку при встре́че.
en: He shook my hand when we met.
note: при встре́че is 'on meeting/when we met', not 'at the meeting' (на встре́че), which invents an event; the sibling sentence already renders При встре́че as 'when we meet'.

ru: Я поза́втракал и пое́хал на рабо́ту.

note: Frame-only collisions: every imperfective partner carries an explicit frequency cue ('every morning', 'at eight', 'usually'), while this one names a single occasion; 'have breakfast' is the only English available.
Frame-only collision with «Зови́ друзе́й на у́жин.»; the objects and destinations differ, so the cue survives.

ru: Я позвала́ бы на по́мощь сосе́дей.

en_alt: Will you allow me to leave the classroom?
note: The Russian leaves the object of позво́лите unstated; English 'allow' requires one, so 'me' is as valid as 'us' and should be accepted.

en_alt: The teacher allowed me to leave the classroom.
note: Same unstated object as the sibling sentence; 'me' is an equally valid reading.

en: I would have allowed you to stay.
note: Perfective бы + past reads best as a single completed non-event; 'would have allowed' forces позво́лить and leaves the imperfective partner as the only plain 'would allow'.

ru: Ле́том мы бу́дем позволя́ть де́тям ложи́ться по́зже.
en_alt: In summer we will allow the children to go to bed later.
note: 'Allow' matches the headword gloss; 'will be letting' would be worse English for a habitual future, so en_gb stays.

ru: Ма́ма позволя́ла нам игра́ть во дворе́.
Пра́вила не позволя́ют шуме́ть в библиоте́ке.

en_alt: Do you allow people to make noise in the library?
note: шуме́ть is a verb; the alt keeps the verbal reading while en_gb stays natural.

ru: Хоро́ший тре́нер не позволя́л бы таки́х оши́бок.
note: The imperfective habitual 'wouldn't allow' is the correct side; the perfective partner is the one being changed to 'would have allowed'.
Already the correct perfective 'would have called'.
Frame-only collisions: each imperfective partner carries a frequency cue ('at any time', 'every day', 'more often') against this single occasion.

ru: Мы поздравля́ем тебя́ с днём рожде́ния!

en_alt: His friends are congratulating him on the victory.
note: Russian present imperfective covers both English presents; the progressive should be accepted.

en_alt: Very pleased to meet you!
note: Equally standard English formula for the greeting.

en: Let me introduce you — this is my friend.
en_alt: Get acquainted, this is my friend.
note: «Познако́мьтесь» used to introduce someone is a formula; 'Get acquainted, …' is translationese, so the literal reading moves to en_alt.

en_alt: We met at a concert.
note: The natural English rendering, accepted alongside the literal one.

ru: Ско́ро ты познако́мишься с но́вым учи́телем.
Ты бы познако́мился с ним ра́ньше.
en_alt: You should have got acquainted with him earlier.
note: «Ты бы + past» with no protasis usually carries the advisory/reproachful sense; both readings should be accepted.

en_alt: Will you inquire about the price of the tickets?
note: Matches the headword gloss and the sibling sentence's wording.

ru: Е́сли бы успе́л, я пойма́л бы мяч.
en: If I had been in time, I would have caught the ball.
en_alt: I would have caught the ball if I had been in time.
note: Perfective single completed event: 'would have caught' forces пойма́ть and leaves the imperfective partner («Я лови́л бы ба́бочек…») as the only 'would catch'; also restores the Russian clause order.

ru: Она́ пошла́ в магази́н за хле́бом.
Я пошла́ бы с тобо́й в кино́.
en_alt: I would go with you to the cinema.
note: Matches the Russian word order; both are natural.
Frame-only collision with «Я ча́сто пока́зываю де́тям ка́рту.», whose 'often' and different objects keep the cue.
Frame-only collision with «Часы́ пока́зывали по́лночь.», which shares no other content; the imperfective side gets a progressive alt instead.

ru: Я показа́ла бы тебе́ э́тот го́род.
note: This side is correct — a single hypothetical showing; the imperfective partner («Ты бы пока́зывала…») is the wrong half and is being changed to 'You should show…'.
The English is right, but 'came into view' is the appear/come-into-sight sense that the headword gloss 'to seem' does not cover — the gloss is probably the half that needs widening.
Same as the sibling: 'will come into view' is accurate but outside the gloss 'to seem'.

Frame-only collision with «Снача́ла э́то бу́дет каза́ться тру́дным.»; English has no progressive for 'seem', so forcing a contrast would produce non-English, and 'the task…easy after practice' is cue enough.
Frame-only collision with «Зада́ча каза́лась лёгкой.», which shares no other content.

ru: Без о́тдыха зада́ча показа́лась бы сло́жной.
en: Without rest the task would have seemed difficult.
note: This is the near-identical half of the collision (partner: «Без подска́зки зада́ча каза́лась бы сло́жной.» — 'would seem'); the perfective бы + past reads as a single completed impression, so 'would have seemed' separates them.

ru: За́втра гид бу́дет пока́зывать нам ста́рый го́род.
note: The compound future is already rendered 'will be showing', which is what the imperfective wants.

ru: Ты бы пока́зывала де́тям бо́льше карти́н.
en: You should show the children more pictures.
note: «Ты бы + past» with no protasis is the advisory construction, not a conditional — 'You would show the children more pictures' is not a sentence an English speaker would write; it also clears the 'would show' collision with показа́ть.

en_alt: The guide shows the tourists the city.
note: Double-object order is equally valid and matches the Russian word order more closely.

en_alt: The clock was showing midnight.
note: The progressive reads the imperfective as the ongoing state it is, and gives the contrast drill a second cue against «Он показа́л биле́т контролёру.»
'Often' already distinguishes it from the perfective imperative partner.

ru: Он то́лько покача́л голово́й в отве́т.
note: покача́ть голово́й is a set collocation and 'shook his head' is its only English; the gloss 'to rock' still underlies it.

ru: Е́сли б он пла́кал, я покача́л бы коля́ску.
en_alt: If he were crying, I would rock the pram.
note: Adds the Russian clause order as an accepted answer.

ru: Ско́ро ба́бушка покача́ет вну́ка в крова́тке.
en: Soon grandmother will rock her grandson in the cot.
en_alt: Soon grandmother will rock the grandson in the cot.
note: вну́к is specifically a grandson; 'grandchild' drops that, and English wants a possessive here.

ru: Я покача́ю коля́ску, пока́ он спит.
Я не поки́нула бы друзе́й в беде́.
Я не поки́ну тебя́ в беде́.

note: 'Turn red' is correct for leaves, but the headword gloss 'to blush' does not cover the plain 'become red' sense — the gloss looks like the narrow half.

ru: Я покрасне́ла бы от тако́й похвалы́.
Я покрасне́ю, е́сли он похва́лит меня́.
Ра́ньше она́ покупа́ла газе́ту ка́ждое у́тро.
С э́того ме́сяца мы бу́дем покупа́ть проду́кты на ры́нке.
note: The compound future is already 'will be buying', which is what бу́дем покупа́ть wants.

ru: Без ски́док я бы покупа́ла ме́ньше.
note: Habitual 'would buy' is exactly right for the imperfective; the perfective partner («я купи́ла бы э́ту маши́ну») is the side that should read 'would have bought'.
Frame-only collision against perfective imperatives; 'I buy … every day' cannot be confused with 'Buy the tickets in advance'.
Frame-only collision against perfective imperatives; the indicative/imperative difference is a plain cue.
